stories.title: High temperature warning issued for most of the country
stories.summary: Met Éireann has issued a Status Yellow high temperature warning for most of the country in the coming days. A warning for counties Clare, Cork, Kerry, Limerick, Galway, and Mayo is currently in place until 7am tomorrow. Another Status Yellow high temperature warning begins at noon tomorrow and is in effect until 6am on Friday. This warning includes Carlow, Kildare, Kilkenny, Laois, Longford, Offaly, Westmeath, Cavan, Donegal, as well as Munster and Connacht.

stories.title: Trump says deal 'still possible' as US strikes Iran
stories.summary: The United States launched a fresh salvo of strikes against Iran, marking a new escalation in the resumption of hostilities, even as US President Donald Trump said a deal with Iran was still possible. "We're going to hit them very hard tonight, and we're going to hit them hard tomorrow," Mr Trump told radio host Hugh Hewitt. Shortly after, US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced strikes had begun at 9.45pm Irish time, the third consecutive night of attacks. "These strikes will continue imposing a heavy cost on Iranian forces and degrade their ability to attack innocent civilians and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz," CENTCOM said.

stories.title: Unions call on Government to end 'costly gimmicks'
stories.summary: The Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU) has called on the Government to end "gimmicks and giveaways" and deliver a budget for workers. In its pre-budget submission, ICTU said it wants to see double indexation of the income tax system to compensate workers for the absence of a tax package for PAYE workers in Budget 2026. It is calling for a €1 increase in the minimum wage, reductions in the cost of using essential public services, an end to the payment cap freeze on pay-related jobseeker's benefit and a timeline for introducing the promised pay-related parent’s benefit. Congress said there also needs to be increased investment in public transport and green energy infrastructure, including targeted supports during winter where necessary.

stories.title: Bill Kenneally survivors to receive State apology
stories.summary: The Government will offer a full and formal State apology to the survivors of paedophile Bill Kenneally today. It comes after a Commission of Investigation found there was a clear and serious dereliction of duty by senior gardaí when they learned Kenneally sexually abused a boy in the late 1980s. Kenneally died in prison last month while serving a 19-year sentence for the historic abuse of boys in Waterford. Taoiseach Micheál Martin will lead the full and formal State apology in the Dáil this afternoon.

stories.title: US immigration agent fatally shoots driver in Maine
stories.summary: A US immigration officer fatally shot a man identified by rights groups as a 26-year-old Colombian, the second such killing by federal agents in less than a week. The shooting happened in Biddeford, a town of 22,000 people in the northern state of Maine, and is likely to fuel criticism of US President Donald Trump's deportation drive and its handling by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Initially, Senator Angus King of Maine told reporters he understood, based on a conversation with Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, that the victim was the subject of an ICE arrest warrant over his immigration status. Yesterday, a spokesperson for Mr King said the senator was told in a second conversation with Mr Mullin that the victim was not the intended target of the warrant.

stories.title: Cabinet to discuss paid leave for early miscarriage
stories.summary: Paid leave is to be provided for the first time for women who suffer an early miscarriage. Minister for Enterprise Peter Burke is to seek Cabinet approval to offer five days of paid leave for women who suffer a miscarriage before 23 weeks of pregnancy. It is believed the same period of sick leave could also be offered to women who have an abortion. The leave would be paid by the employer. Bringing the bill to Cabinet, Mr Burke will tell his ministerial colleagues that women often do not have the choice to take time to grieve and recover from a miscarriage.
